## VERDICT (one paragraph, honest)
**CLAIM-0015 is FALSIFIED at L0 — a CLEAN, PUBLISHABLE KILL, on the LOAD-BEARING gate RE-1, in both corpora.**
The single-token d=1 acceptance collapse is real and replicated (out-of-sample d=1 accept 0.024 CC / 0.057 Codex
vs interior baseline 0.256 / 0.271), but the payload's FORMAT CLASS does NOT add predictive value over a
length+entropy JOINT baseline — it is in fact WEAKER. dAUC(format - length+entropy joint) = -0.090 (CC,
95% CI [-0.400,+0.155]) and -0.322 (Codex, 95% CI [-0.450,-0.164]); the pre-registered PASS required the 95%
LOWER bound > 0, which fails in both (significantly negative in Codex). The length+entropy joint logistic
predicts the rare d=1 accepts BETTER than format class (AUC 0.571 / 0.897 vs format 0.480 / 0.575). This is
exactly the pre-registered null: **"JSON is hard" reduces to "long rare-token-heavy payloads are hard"**
(consistent with Sennrich/BPE: non-prose payloads tokenize into rarer subword sequences captured by
length+entropy). Format-class also fails to beat draft-entropy thresholding (RE-7: Codex dAUC -0.353
CI[-0.432,-0.273]; draft-entropy AUC 0.928), so there is no model-free pre-draft advantage over the existing
adaptive-SD family (SVIP/TALON/SpecBound/Nightjar). The d=1 cost is NOT >=80% concentrated (RE-6 share 0.559
CC / 0.180 Codex, lower bounds 0.349 / 0.122 << 0.80). The only positive — RE-3, a small genuine
format-transition component in CC (non-prose dips +0.045 more than prose, CI[+0.009,+0.111]) — does NOT
replicate in Codex (gap -0.057) and is redundant with length+entropy for prediction. The surviving deliverable
is the format-BLIND fallback (RE-5): suppressing the d=1 draft unconditionally recovers ~15.6% (CC) / ~18.6%
(Codex) of per-turn WASTED draft FLOPs at PROVABLY zero accuracy cost. **No L1 GPU spend is motivated for the
format-class pre-draft gating hypothesis.**

## DATA (RE-2)
- Claude Code: 78 usable sessions (>=50 asst tokens & >=1 tool result). Within-corpus cross-fit split: fit=40, eval=38.
- Codex: 80 usable sessions. split: fit=46, eval=34.
- Out-of-sample protocol: trigram predictor trained on one half, transitions of the OTHER half labelled by it
  (accept = draft top-1 == realized token). Models (format-rate table, len+ent logistic, draft-ent logistic)
  FIT on the fit-half transitions; AUC/dAUC EVALUATED on the disjoint eval-half; cluster-bootstrap over eval
  sessions (B=2000, seed 20260601). >=2 corpora satisfied (CC + Codex).
- Eval tool->assistant transitions: CC 293, Codex 106. d=1 accepts (positives) are SPARSE — see per-class n below.

## RE-1 [LOAD-BEARING] — format-class AUC vs LENGTH+ENTROPY JOINT  ==> FAILS (PRIMARY KILL)
Paired cluster-bootstrap dAUC = AUC(M_format) - AUC(M_lenent), eval half, B=2000.
| corpus | AUC(format) | AUC(len+ent joint) | dAUC | 95% CI | PASS (LB>0) |
|--------|-------------|--------------------|------|--------|-------------|
| CC     | 0.4805 | 0.5709 | **-0.0904** | [-0.3997, +0.1552] | **NO** |
| Codex  | 0.5750 | 0.8967 | **-0.3217** | [-0.4501, -0.1636] | **NO (sig. negative)** |
Format-class does NOT add predictive value over the length+entropy joint; it is weaker in both corpora and
significantly weaker in Codex. Per the locked decision rule (sec 4 RE-1) this is the CLEAN HONEST KILL: the
novelty dies into the length+entropy-explained / confidence-gated family.

## RE-7 — format-class vs draft-entropy head-to-head (full ROC)  ==> FAILS
dAUC = AUC(M_format) - AUC(M_draftent); FDR/FNR at train-Youden threshold of the format suppression rule.
| corpus | AUC(format) | AUC(draft-ent) | dAUC | 95% CI | FDR | FNR |
|--------|-------------|----------------|------|--------|-----|-----|
| CC     | 0.4805 | 0.3884 | +0.0922 | [-0.3829, +0.4063] (incl 0) | 0.0197 | 0.4790 |
| Codex  | 0.5750 | 0.9283 | -0.3533 | [-0.4320, -0.2734] | 0.0000 | 0.7600 |
Format-class cannot be shown to beat draft-entropy thresholding (CC CI includes 0; Codex draft-entropy
strongly dominates, AUC 0.928). No model-free PRE-draft advantage over the adaptive-SD family (SVIP 2411.18462
/ TALON 2601.07353 / SpecBound 2604.12247 / Nightjar 2512.22420). The low FDR (~0-2%) just reflects that almost
every d=1 token is rejected (suppression is almost always "correct") — i.e. the blind rule already works.

## RE-6 — >=80% d=1 concentration  ==> FAILS
share = |cost_1| / sum_{d=1..8}|cost_d|, cost_d = interior_acc - accept(d). Bootstrap lower bound must be >0.80.
| corpus | share point | 95% CI | PASS (LB>0.80) |
|--------|-------------|--------|-----------------|
| CC     | 0.5593 | [0.3488, 0.6126] | **NO** |
| Codex  | 0.1804 | [0.1223, 0.2529] | **NO** |
The d=1 cost is NOT >=80% concentrated under the (conservative, pre-registered) |.|-denominator rule. In Codex
the post-tool d>=3 tokens are MORE predictable than interior (formulaic resumptions), so the |cost| at d>=2
dominates the denominator and the d=1 share collapses to 0.18 — corroborating EXP-0046.

## RE-3 — matched-format prose->prose splice control  ==> CC PASS / Codex FAIL (not robust)
gap = mean(accept_d1 | prose-control) - mean(accept_d1 | nonprose); prose-control = prose tool-results + user->asst.
| corpus | prose d1 | nonprose d1 | gap | 95% CI | PASS (LB>0) |
|--------|----------|-------------|-----|--------|-------------|
| CC     | 0.0588 | 0.0135 | +0.0453 | [+0.0090, +0.1108] | **YES** |
| Codex  | 0.0000 | 0.0571 | -0.0571 | [-0.0990, -0.0190] | **NO (sign-flipped)** |
INTERPRETATION: CC shows a *genuine* small format-transition component (the first prose token after a NON-prose
payload is harder than after prose), so the effect is NOT pure generic discontinuity in CC. BUT (a) it does not
replicate in Codex (where prose tool-results are essentially absent, n=1, and stdout d=1 accept is actually
higher), and (b) it is REDUNDANT with length+entropy for prediction (RE-1) — length already encodes that
non-prose payloads are longer/higher-entropy. A real-but-prediction-useless effect.

## RE-5 — FLOPs recovered (explicit denominator) + exactness  ==> surviving format-BLIND deliverable
- Denominator (locked): per-turn WASTED draft FLOPs = sum_{d=1..8} P(reject@d) (one wasted draft forward per
  rejected speculated position). recovered-by-d1-suppression = P(reject@d1) / sum_d P(reject@d).
| corpus | P(reject@d1) | recovered fraction of wasted draft FLOPs | 95% CI |
|--------|--------------|------------------------------------------|--------|
| CC     | 0.9761 | 0.1555 | [0.1503, 0.1646] |
| Codex  | 0.9434 | 0.1859 | [0.1774, 0.1948] |
- FLOP-cost-model sweep: with draft:verify param ratio rho in {1/8,1/4}, the d=1 draft forward is rho per token;
  unconditionally suppressing it removes that forward on EVERY turn while it is rejected ~95-98% of the time, so
  the false-suppression cost is ~2-6% of one draft forward per turn (negligible).
- EXACTNESS ARGUMENT (formal): SD is exact iff suppression changes ONLY the draft length, not the verifier
  input. Suppressing the d=1 draft = draft_length 0 for that step; the verifier then decodes that token itself
  from the identical context, so the output distribution equals vanilla decoding of that token. Therefore the
  suppression is provably accuracy-neutral (confirmed trivially at draft_length=0: verifier reproduces its own
  next token). The recovered fraction is a real, model-FREE, format-BLIND saving — the publishable fallback
  named in VERDICT-0054 baseline_requirements ("always suppress d=1" — simpler/thinner but valid).

## RE-8 — classification overhead vs single-token draft forward
- Regex format classifier: **89.89 us / payload** (median of 3 reps over 4571 tool-result payloads), pure
  /usr/bin/python3 stdlib on Mac CPU.
- Comparison band: a real small ngram/EAGLE draft forward at H100 scale is ~O(50us-1ms). 89.9us sits at the
  LOW-to-MIDDLE of that band, i.e. classification costs roughly AS MUCH as the draft forward it would save.
  Combined with RE-1 (format-class adds no predictive value), the model-free advantage is ILLUSORY/MOOT. A
  compiled classifier would be faster, but there is nothing to gate on. (The L1 lane would need a real
  draft-forward microbench to settle this precisely; not motivated here.)

## CAVEATS / PROXY LIMITS (honest)
- Trigram top-1-agreement PROXY, NOT a real SD draft/target pair (no torch/HF cache on node). 2-token context =
  conservative boundary/format sensitivity. The proxy provides NO positive evidence for a format-class
  predictive advantage and shows the part it CAN detect is fully absorbed by length+entropy.
- Extreme positive-class imbalance at d=1 (2-6%) makes AUCs noisy. The kill is robust to this because (a) the
  point estimates favour length+entropy in BOTH corpora, (b) Codex is significantly negative, (c) the
  in-sample format separation does not survive out-of-sample, and (d) cross-corpus confirms.
- Codex prose tool-results are near-absent (n=1 eval), so the RE-3 prose control there leans on user turns;
  reported honestly as underpowered.
- Single node, single proxy. The revival condition is a real neural SD draft/target pair (L1) showing format-
  class dAUC over length+entropy joint with CI>0 — which this L0 gate does NOT motivate spending on.
